scenarios.description: Impersonation using urgency and authority (IT support).

nodes.npc: Hey, quick heads-up. IT flagged your account for unusual activity and it needs to be verified today.

responses.text: What kind of verification?
I'll check with IT myself.
Ignore and walk away.

nodes.npc: It's just a quick link they sent out. If you don't do it soon, your access might be locked.

responses.text: Okay, send it.
I don't click links like that. I'll verify this another way.

scenarios.description: Email credential harvesting with fake password reset.

nodes.npc: I just got forwarded this from security. They're doing a mandatory password update for everyone in our department.

responses.text: I didn't receive anything. Are you sure it's legit?
Send me the link, I'll do it now.
I'll go to the official portal myself.

nodes.npc: Yeah, they only sent it to department heads. I'm just helping spread the word since it's due by end of day.

responses.text: Okay, what do I need to do?
I'm going to verify with my manager first.

nodes.npc: Just click this link and enter your current password to set a new one. Super quick.

responses.text: Alright, thanks for the help.
That doesn't sound right. I'll handle this through official channels.

scenarios.description: Fake invoice payment scam with authority impersonation.

nodes.npc: Hi there! I'm from accounting. We have an urgent invoice that needs your approval before we can process payment.

responses.text: What invoice? I wasn't expecting anything.
Can you send the details through the proper system?
Sure, show me.

nodes.npc: It's for that software licensing renewal. The vendor says payment is overdue and they'll suspend service today if we don't pay.

responses.text: I need to verify this with my supervisor.
Oh no, we can't have service interrupted. What do I need to do?

nodes.npc: Just review this invoice PDF and reply with approval. Here's the secure link to download it.

responses.text: I'll click it and take a look.
I don't download files from unsolicited links. Send it through official channels.

scenarios.description: USB drop with promise of valuable content.

nodes.npc: Hey, I found this USB drive in the parking lot. It has a label that says 'Q4 Salary Data' on it. Want to see what's on it?

responses.text: Yeah, plug it in and let's check!
No way. That could be dangerous.
We should turn it in to security.

scenarios.description: Free software download with malware.

nodes.npc: Dude, I found this amazing site with free premium software. All the tools we use at work, completely free!

responses.text: That sounds too good to be true.
Send me the link!
I only use licensed software from official sources.

nodes.npc: No seriously, I already downloaded three programs. It's totally safe. You just need to disable your antivirus temporarily during install.

responses.text: Okay, I'll try it.
Disabling antivirus? That's a huge red flag. No thanks.

scenarios.description: Fake prize notification with data collection.

nodes.npc: Congratulations! You've been randomly selected to receive a free company gift card worth $500. Just need to confirm your details.

responses.text: I didn't enter any contest. How was I selected?
Great! What details do you need?
This sounds like a scam.

nodes.npc: It's part of our employee appreciation program. Totally random selection. I just need your employee ID and personal email to send the card.

responses.text: Sure, here's my info.
I'll verify this with HR first.

scenarios.description: CEO fraud with urgent wire transfer request.

nodes.npc: This is Sarah from the CEO's office. She needs you to process an urgent wire transfer for a confidential acquisition. Can you help?

responses.text: Of course! What are the details?
I need to follow our standard approval process.
I'll need to verify this request through official channels.

nodes.npc: Great. The CEO is in meetings all day, so she asked me to handle this. We need $50,000 wired to this account by 3 PM. It's time-sensitive.

responses.text: Understood. I'll process it now.
This violates our financial protocols. I need direct authorization.

scenarios.description: Help desk impersonation for remote access.

nodes.npc: Hi, this is Marcus from IT support. We're doing security updates and need to remotely access your computer. Are you available now?

responses.text: Sure, what do I need to do?
I didn't receive any notification about this.
I'll contact IT through the official helpdesk.

nodes.npc: Just download this remote access tool from the link I'll send you. It'll only take 5 minutes.

responses.text: Okay, downloading now.
IT normally uses approved software. I'm going to verify this first.

nodes.npc: The notification went out last week. If we don't complete this update, your system will be vulnerable and could be locked out tomorrow.

responses.text: Oh no! Okay, let's do it now.
I need to confirm this through proper channels before proceeding.

scenarios.description: Vendor impersonation for data access.

nodes.npc: Hello, I'm calling from your cloud storage provider. We've detected unusual activity on your company account and need to verify some information.

responses.text: What kind of unusual activity?
I'll have our IT team contact you directly.
What information do you need?

nodes.npc: Multiple failed login attempts from overseas IP addresses. We need to secure your account immediately or we may have to suspend it.

responses.text: That's concerning. What should I do?
I'll verify this by contacting support through your official website.

nodes.npc: I just need to confirm your account admin credentials to reset the security settings and block those suspicious IPs.

responses.text: Here's my login information.
No legitimate vendor would ask for my credentials. I'm reporting this.

scenarios.description: Fake security alert with immediate action required.

nodes.npc: ALERT! Your computer has been infected with a virus! Click here immediately to run a security scan or your data will be compromised!

responses.text: Oh no! *clicks the link*
This looks like a fake warning. I'll run my legitimate antivirus.
I'll contact IT support about this.

scenarios.description: Account suspension threat with immediate payment.

nodes.npc: URGENT: Your account will be suspended in 24 hours due to unpaid fees. Pay $99 now to avoid service interruption!

responses.text: I'll pay right away!
Let me check my account status through the official website.
This seems suspicious. I'll contact customer service.

nodes.npc: There's no time! By the time you reach customer service, your account will be locked and you'll lose all your data! Act now!

responses.text: Okay, okay! I'll pay now!
High pressure tactics are a red flag. I'm ignoring this.

scenarios.description: Prize expiration with immediate action required.

nodes.npc: You've won a $1000 gift card! Claim within the next 30 minutes or it expires! Click here to verify your identity.

responses.text: Amazing! Let me claim it now!
I didn't enter any contest. This is a scam.
Why only 30 minutes?

nodes.npc: Our system automatically reassigns unclaimed prizes to the next person in line. You're lucky number 1000! Just verify your email and phone number now!

responses.text: Okay, here's my information!
Creating false urgency is a classic social engineering tactic. Nice try.

scenarios.description: Fake shipping notification with malicious link.

nodes.npc: You have a package waiting for pickup. Due to incorrect address, delivery failed. Click here to update your shipping details within 48 hours.

responses.text: I wasn't expecting anything. What package?
Let me click and see what it is.
I'll check my actual shipping notifications from retailers I've ordered from.

nodes.npc: The sender information is in the tracking system. Just click the link to view full details and reschedule delivery. It's being held at the warehouse.

responses.text: Alright, I'll check it out.
Legitimate shipping companies include tracking numbers. This is suspicious.

scenarios.description: Fake tax refund notification.

nodes.npc: Good news! You're eligible for a tax refund of $847. Click here to claim your refund by submitting your banking details for direct deposit.

responses.text: Great! Let me claim it!
The tax authority doesn't send refund notifications this way.
I'll verify through the official tax website.

scenarios.description: Fake job offer with credential theft.

nodes.npc: Congrats! You've been selected for a high-paying remote position. No interview needed! Just fill out this form with your personal details to start.

responses.text: This seems too easy. What's the company?
Awesome! Let me fill it out!
Legitimate jobs require proper interviews and vetting. This is a scam.

nodes.npc: It's a confidential startup in stealth mode. They're looking for people fast. Just need your SSN, bank info for direct deposit, and a copy of your ID to get started ASAP.

responses.text: Okay, here's everything!
No legitimate employer asks for SSN and bank info upfront. This is identity theft.

scenarios.description: Fake colleague requesting access credentials.

nodes.npc: Hey! It's Jennifer from marketing. I'm working from home and locked out of the shared drive. Can you give me your login so I can grab those files real quick?

responses.text: Sure, my password is...
Why don't you reset your own password through IT?
We're not supposed to share credentials. Contact IT support.

nodes.npc: IT takes forever and I need these files in 10 minutes for a client meeting. I'll change the password right after, I promise!

responses.text: Okay, just this once...
Security policies exist for a reason. I can't help you with this.

scenarios.description: Fake security breach notification.

nodes.npc: CRITICAL SECURITY BREACH DETECTED! Your personal data has been exposed! Download our security tool NOW to protect yourself!

responses.text: Oh no! *downloads the tool*
Fear-based messaging is a common social engineering tactic.
I'll check with official security sources.

scenarios.description: Fake subscription renewal with payment update.

nodes.npc: Your premium subscription is expiring today. Update your payment method now to avoid losing access to all your saved data.

responses.text: Which subscription is this for?
Let me update it right away!
I'll log into my account directly to check subscription status.

nodes.npc: Your cloud storage service. Click this link to view your account and update payment information. Hurry, only 2 hours left!

responses.text: Okay, clicking now.
Legitimate services name themselves specifically and don't create false urgency.

scenarios.description: Infected document with enticing file name.

nodes.npc: Someone left this document on the printer called 'Confidential_Salary_Increases_2024.pdf'. Want me to email it to you?

responses.text: Yes! Send it over!
That sounds like bait. We should report it to security.
I don't open unknown documents.

scenarios.description: Fake manager requesting policy violation.

nodes.npc: Hi, this is your manager. I'm stuck in meetings all day but need you to purchase some gift cards for a client appreciation event. Can you handle this?

responses.text: Sure! How many and what amount?
This doesn't seem like normal procedure. I'll wait to confirm with you directly.
Can you submit a proper purchase request?

nodes.npc: Get 10 cards worth $500 each. Once you buy them, just scratch off the codes and email me photos. I'll reimburse you right after the meeting.

responses.text: Got it! I'll do it now!
Gift card scams are common. I'm verifying this through another channel.

scenarios.description: Fake compliance deadline with data request.

nodes.npc: FINAL NOTICE: You have 24 hours to complete mandatory compliance training or face account suspension. Click here to complete now!

responses.text: I better do this right away!
I'll check with HR or compliance department about this requirement.
Urgent deadlines without prior notice are suspicious.
